extracted.intended_audience: Authors (and contributors/editors) submitting manuscripts to medical journals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for completing and handling the ICMJE Disclosure of Interest form and the broader expectation that authors transparently disclose financial and non‑financial relationships and activities that could constitute conflicts of interest across all stages of research and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of completed disclosure form
rubrics_metrics.description: Your completed form is NOT to be submitted to the ICMJE and it cannot be saved to the ICMJE website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Save the form on your own computer and check with the journal you are submitting to for specific instructions on how to submit your completed form to them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of conflicts of interest across the research and publication lifecycle
rubrics_metrics.description: Public trust in the scientific process and the credibility of published articles depend in part on how transparently conflicts of interest are handled during the planning, implementation, writing, peer review, editing, and publication of scientific work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors (and contributors/editors/reviewers) should disclose relevant interests so that conflicts can be assessed and managed throughout all stages of the work; see ICMJE Recommendations and FAQs for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure scope — financial and non‑financial relationships and activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure of Financial and Non-Financial Relationships and Activities, and Conflicts of Interest (as a distinct category of responsibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosures should cover both financial and non‑financial relationships and activities that could constitute conflicts of interest; consult the ICMJE Disclosure Forms and Recommendations for specifics on what to report.
